variants.headline: Looking back: ordered goods reach the dock
variants.sub: Imported {good} ordered by {company} has landed at the colony's port.
variants.body:
We return to our earlier coverage. Our report recorded this: The company {company} had received its imported order of {good} at the port.

People live through the interval between an order and its arrival. Labour should keep that ordinary perspective in view when discussing imports. Goods matter through the lives they serve; a completed delivery deserves attention without making the person who needs provision disappear behind the commercial account.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

The handling of {target} merits scrutiny through the completed delivery. The order has landed and been paid for; the long interval is part of the practical record, not a detail to overlook.
